svg.text: Audi seat controller - enclosure wiring (bench layout, buck beside the Nano)
Hammond 1599HBK | J1 seat side: switch panel + pushbutton (9-pin) | J2 power side: 12V in + 2 motor outputs (9-pin) | not to scale

g.text: Button powers the module: pressed, it
puts 12V on DC+. IN is jumpered to DC+
(positive trigger). Mode P-3: relay on for
the set time, then off. Bench-tested.
linked to J1-7 on the block

svg.text: Inside the box wires are coloured by job. Outside J1 they are the pushbutton's real wire colours. Thin wires are 22 AWG; the KF2510 cable is 26 AWG. Not to scale.
Wiring list - tick each one off as you wire it
Switch panel to Nano (22 AWG, 5V logic only)
parked - front tilt, no driver yet
parked - rear tilt, no driver yet
Pushbutton (22 AWG, 12V only - never to a Nano pin)
J1-7 short link on the block
LED fed from the NO line
feed is fused at F1 before J2
Pushbutton rear view - 5-wire plug (colours read from your photos)
yellow NC -> not used - insulate the end
Not from a datasheet - confirm with a meter (checklist step 1) before relying on it.
Safety notes - numbered markers on the diagram
The button does not signal the Nano. Pressing it puts +12V on the module's own DC+ supply; IN is jumpered to DC+ (the maker lists IN as a
positive, high-level trigger). In mode P-3 the relay closes at once, stays on for the set time, then opens and stays off. Bench-tested (README).
F1 sits in the +12V feed before J2-5, as close to the supply as possible. Its rating is set from the motors' measured stall current and must not
exceed what 16 AWG wire can carry - not yet decided (README open item). F2 is 1A on the buck converter's red input lead.
The Cytron MDD10A has no reverse-polarity protection: B+ must get the switched +12V from YYLOCK NO, B- must go to ground. Check before
power-up. The YYLOCK relay is labelled 30A, but the module has not been tested at the motors' stall current yet.
For about a second while the Nano boots, D5/D6 float. R1/R2 (10k) hold PWM1/PWM2 low, and PWM low = motor stopped whatever DIR
is (Cytron manual). Solder them across the cable wires at the Cytron plug and heat-shrink. The firmware then drives the pins LOW in setup().
J1-1 to J1-5: switch panel, 5V logic, to the Nano. J1-6 to J1-9: pushbutton, 12V, to the YYLOCK/J2 only. No pushbutton wire
goes to a Nano pin. The only thing on the Nano's 5V pin is the buck converter's regulated 5V output.
All grounds meet at the WAGO (5 ports): Cytron B-, Nano GND, buck input -, J2-6 GND in, YYLOCK DC-. Nano analog-row GND: switch PIN 4 +
buck output -. Nano digital-row GND: KF2510 orange + wire to the WAGO. YYLOCK DC-: WAGO wire + button LED-.
Wires per screw terminal (count them when you check)
YYLOCK DC+: 3 (button NO, self-latch, IN jumper) | YYLOCK NO: 3 (Cytron B+, self-latch, F2/buck) | COM: 1 | IN: 1 (jumper)
YYLOCK DC-: 2 (WAGO, LED-) | J1-7: 2 (button NO, link) | J2-5 inside: 2 (COM, button C) | Nano GND pins: 2 each | WAGO: 1 per port
1 Button: with the plug on, meter blue-green beeps only while pressed; blue-yellow beeps when released. Diode test red/black to find LED +.
2 Check every row of the wiring list by continuity, terminal to terminal, and tick it. Tug-test every screw terminal and WAGO lever.
3 No supply connected: J2-5 to J2-6 must NOT read near 0 ohms. Cytron B+ to B- must not read near 0 ohms.
4 Fit F1 (rating decided from stall current) and F2 (1A). Confirm the vehicle feed polarity at the J2 plug before connecting it.
5 First power-up with motor plugs J2-1..4 disconnected: press the button - relay clicks, Nano LED on, Nano 5V pin reads 4.75-5.25V.
6 Still without motors: meter M1A-M1B and M2A-M2B read 0V at rest, about 12V only while a seat switch is held, 0V again on release.
7 Connect the motors and test each direction; confirm the 8 s run cutoff and that the YYLOCK switches everything off after its set time.
